overclaims: Noncoders have documented launches with real users and several integrated features.
checks.note: Quote, conditions, axis/horizon/outcome and citations are fine. The rationale's opening says 'launches', plural, with real users. Only e1 (Plinq) is a launch, and its user figures are Lovable's own unverified report. e2 describes a prototype built mainly for its owner ('useful for one person'), not a launch. 'Documented' also overstates a vendor-reported account. The sentence should name the single vendor-reported launch.

The proposition sets aside the 'they never let you know' framing, as the contract says to. e1 (Feb 24 2025) establishes that Cursor used Claude, and the explanation's note of complaints in the thread fits the evidence. The limitation about unretrievable forum records matches the packet (Cursor forum fragment, Reddit 403). The unresolved historical_observation matches the reviews.

The 'my understanding is' hedge is kept. The UK census (available 2024-06-13) and RSNA (2024-12-05) items support the shortage part. The North Denmark item is described accurately as partial task substitution with doctors moved to other work. The rationale correctly says that finding no displacement case does not prove there were none. Excerpts, dates and relations are correct.

'Hype about AI coding' paraphrases 'naive enthusiasm from people like Roose' in line with Marcus's own 'if hype deters kids' in context and the contract's interpretation. The Feb 2025 fieldwork is before the post, so 'pre-forecast' is accurate even though publication was 2025-03-12. The limitations state the survey's scope correctly. The open-horizon unresolved outcome matches the reviews.
